title_original: PHOTO-ART Paris 2026 / Contemporary Perspectives on Fine Art Photography

blocks.text: Against a backdrop of profound change in our cultural and environmental reference points, PHOTO ART PARIS is launching its first edition with this aim: to position fine art photography as a central medium for interpreting the contemporary world. This exhibition brings together 13 photographers with distinctive visual styles, drawn from a variety of artistic and cultural backgrounds. Each work on display reflects a unique artistic approach, whilst contributing to a collective narrative centred on key themes: our relationship with living things, memory, territories and human interactions. Four contemporary sculptors complement this exhibition with original works, introducing a three-dimensional perspective that resonates directly with the photographic works on display. The 2026 edition is distinguished by the presence of Olivier Grunewald as artist of honour. His work, internationally recognised for its ability to reveal the aesthetic power of natural phenomena, forms the very essence of this inaugural edition and reinforces its artistic credibility. Conceived as a platform where creativity and the art market converge, PHOTO ART PARIS is aimed at a discerning audience: collectors, businesses, patrons, institutions and cultural influencers. The exhibition offers: • A selection of fine art works available for purchase • A structured curatorial itinerary designed to facilitate the interpretation and understanding of artistic approaches • Highlights: a VIP opening, meet-and-greets, talks and book signings by exhibiting artists and a number of guest artists • A catalogue presenting all the artists and works

Beyond the exhibition itself, PHOTO ART PARIS aims to establish a permanent fixture on the Parisian cultural scene, with plans for annual expansion contingent upon the success of this inaugural edition.
Practical information November 18th – 29th Venue: Galerie 24B – 24 Bis, rue Saint-Roch – 75001 Paris
The works on display will be available for purchase, enabling collectors and art lovers to acquire original pieces and extend the experience beyond the exhibition.
